title: Scan Matrix
body:
How a keyboard detects keypresses without one wire per key. The keys are wired as a grid
of rows and columns; the keyboard controller drives one row at a time and reads which
columns come back closed. The intersection identifies the key, so $n$ rows and $m$ columns
cover $n \times m$ keys with $n + m$ wires.

Scanning the whole grid repeatedly is what turns a key going down or coming up into a
[[Make-Break Codes|make or break code]]. See [[IKBD Systems]].
